[{"id": "wMnJQCKVJz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf10Website Manual", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3AYPXvjrxi", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Churchit gives your church two places on the internet. The website is public: anyone can read it without a login. It fills itself from your records, so when you publish a sermon, a belief, a missionary or an event, it shows on the website at once. The member portal is a private app for your members, where each person sees their own household, sign-ups, giving and groups.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3Ib1gMPrTs", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Users with the Church Manager role profile can change the website. They have the Website Manager role, which a Church Branch Manager does not have. Members and visitors need no training: the website and the member portal work on any phone or computer.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "n1zRu-BrKk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Web Site workspace shows the number of web pages, a chart of web pages by type and a preview of your home page. Click the preview to open the website in a new tab. The sidebar lists Web Pages, Web Forms, Website Settings, Website Themes, About Us Settings and Contact Us Settings. Portal Settings, Website Script, Website Sidebars and Website Route Meta are in the Setup folder.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "irzLScBtD_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83c\udf0eWebsite", "col": 12}}, {"id": "L9oI_KFd_e", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Your website starts with these pages: Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions, Ministries, Find a Group, Calendar, About Us, Contact Us and Give. Most of them list your records. A record shows on the website only when you tick Publish on it:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "0C3Dd7Z81T", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Beliefs: the published Beliefs.
- Sermons: the published sermons, the newest first (see the Study manual).
- Missions: the published missionaries that are not Inactive and not Sensitive (see the Missions manual).
- Ministries: the published ministries whose status is Active.
- Calendar: the published functions (see Calendar below).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "35qVbI1B96", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: A visitor tells you that the youth ministry is missing from your website. Open the Ministry: Publish is not ticked. Tick it and save. The Ministries page and the home page show the youth ministry at once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TEE79WuGpa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Other pages: Announcements (/announcements) shows the announcements of the newest published bulletins that share them. Bulletins (/bulletins) is for signed-in members. Watch Live (/live) shows your live stream. Locations lists your churches when you have more than one. The Connection Card, the prayer request form for visitors and other forms are Web Forms.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "raM0fwGGAM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Change a page", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FpHY-7H_QE", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each page that Churchit ships (Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions and Ministries) is a Web Page record that you can edit. An upgrade of Churchit keeps your wording. It only repairs the part of a page that reads your records.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KkE5VLSqvJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open the page under Web Pages. The content is in Main Section (HTML). It is a template that reads your published records, so the page stays up to date by itself. To write a page by hand instead, change Content Type to Rich Text or Markdown. Put styles for one page in the Custom CSS tab. The look of the whole site is the Website Theme.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "FQFGjkSvDJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To make a new page, click Add Web Page, write it and tick Published. Publishing a page adds it to the end of the website menu. Un-publishing or deleting a page removes its links from the menu and the footer. A message confirms each change. Only publishing adds a menu item: editing a page that is already published does not add it again.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Umr6ZdExRL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Which fields the public can see", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uLMKp4zaR0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "In the desk, a small badge beside a field label shows that the field appears outside the desk. An outgoing-link badge means anyone can see it. A people badge means only signed-in members can see it. Point at the badge to see which pages show the field, and click it to open one. On a phone, tap the badge.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-6TiR4uhcl", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: On a Missionary form, the badge beside Photo says that the Missions page shows it to anyone. Before you add a photo of a missionary in a closed country, you know that the public would see it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eiBwk2FE7E", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddedThe Website Menu and Footer", "col": 12}}, {"id": "shx4JuxQYU", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The website menu is the Top Bar Items table in Website Settings, on the Navbar tab. Some pages are not in the menu at first, for example Announcements (/announcements) and Watch Live (/live). To add one:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "O0eOr-sZbM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "1. Open Website Settings and click the Navbar tab.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dGwEbMQjTa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "2. In the Top Bar Items table, click Add Row.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kRcr8gI9bS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "3. In Label, type the name to show in the menu, for example Watch Live.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "HLFeFlE4kV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "4. In URL, type the address of the page, for example /live.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "dJuftH19xb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "5. Click the edit icon at the end of the row and tick Align Right, so that the item shows next to the other items. The items that Churchit installs have this box ticked. An item that Churchit adds when you publish a page does not, so tick it on that item too.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xsWphr6XT9", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "6. Drag the row up or down to move the item, then save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "z-L3YFA_y1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "With more than one church, a menu item opens the page of the church that the visitor chose. When you remove a link from the menu, the page stays online. After you save, Churchit offers to un-publish each Web Page that the link opened. Answer No to keep the page open by its address. When a page is off in Church Features, the menu hides its item.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gijL8uLBXd", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Logo", "col": 12}}, {"id": "bzmh6tVE3v", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To show your logo in the menu bar, open the Navbar tab of Website Settings and set Brand Image. The menu bar then shows the logo in place of the church name. This works only while Brand HTML is empty.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cJ8-IXbRFu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Footer", "col": 12}}, {"id": "uUVFHd6ipF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Every page ends with a short footer. It shows the church name and founding year from the Church record, the phone number from Contact Us Settings, the church address (it opens in OpenStreetMap), and the copyright from the Footer tab of Website Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NwyEEZNFUJ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The footer links are I'm New (the Connection Card), Prayer Request (the prayer request form for visitors) and Member Portal. Change them in the Footer Items table on the Footer tab of Website Settings. When a page is off in Church Features, its link goes too. If you remove all the footer links on purpose, an update of Churchit does not put them back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "A9KyF7qT2R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The login page also shows the footer, with help on how to get a login from the church office and a link to fill in a Connection Card. To hide it, clear Show Footer on Login in Website Settings.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2oYHMoeHDn", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "About Us and Contact Us", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MMW7f6ZFoe", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The About Us page shows the About text and the Mission Statement of the Church record, and the History and Team Members from About Us Settings. The introduction in About Us Settings shows only when the Church has no About text. Write your main introduction on the About tab of the Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cVkQHhDKcB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Contact Us page shows the church address, unless you tick Contact address differs from the church address in Contact Us Settings and type another one. A message from the contact form goes to Forward To Email in Contact Us Settings, or to the email of the Church when that is empty.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "MScuP5EpzX", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Each message is also kept on the Church: open the Church and look at its activity at the bottom of the form. When Send Acknowledgement Email is ticked, the visitor gets a short thank-you email. One visitor can send at most 10 messages an hour.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Q__HYP-E35", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcc5Calendar", "col": 12}}, {"id": "yJcMnaqj3k", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The Calendar page shows your published functions. A function with Link Only ticked is not on the calendar, the feed or the home page, but anyone with its link can still open it. On a phone, the Calendar opens as a list of the events of the month: tap month to see the grid. Click an event to open its details. A function with Streamed ticked shows a Watch live button while it runs.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PKYxmHb-Ta", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Two buttons above the calendar share it:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KPNNPb_kI2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Subscribe adds the calendar to the calendar app of a phone or computer. Calendar apps check it for changes by themselves.
- Download .ics saves the calendar as a file.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "kpYPRshY9c", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The feed holds the published functions from one month ago to six months ahead, with their address, description and online meeting link. It shows the calendar of the church that the page shows, without its branch churches.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tubjm2uX2L", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To share the calendar of one church or one ministry, copy the Subscribe link and add to its end:
- church= and the ID of a published church, to show only that church, for example ?church=CHR-01.
- ministry= and the name of a published ministry, to show only its functions, for example ?church=CHR-01&ministry=Youth. A ministry that is not published gives an empty calendar.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4VSBGA3tS4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Put ? before the first addition and & before the next one.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9g0Pzc1v1B", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcfaWatch Live", "col": 12}}, {"id": "OkRk0YhOkj", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To show your live stream on the website, open the Church, and in the Contact section of the Details tab, put the link to the stream in Live Stream Link. The link must start with https://. The /live page then shows the stream:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-0UnhGG3OY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A YouTube video link, a youtube.com/channel/ link that ends in /live, a Let's Church media link, a PeerTube video link or an Owncast player link (it ends in /embed/video) plays on the page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "3GRGQF0qeb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Any other link, such as a youtube.com/@name/live link, opens the site of the stream.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "6TicDd_9hV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A branch church without its own link uses the link of its parent church. If no church has a link, /live shows \"Page not found\".", "col": 12}}, {"id": "UNNsPf1jRK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The menu has no Watch Live item at first. To add one, see The Website Menu and Footer, and use the URL /live.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "GAxwrMHgE7", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Stream from a YouTube channel. A youtube.com/@name/live link opens YouTube and does not play on your page. Use the link with your channel ID instead: https://www.youtube.com/channel/channel ID/live. A channel ID starts with UC. To find it, sign in to YouTube with the channel account and open https://www.youtube.com/account_advanced, then copy the Channel ID. This link always plays the stream that is live now, so you do not change it for each service.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ocYwCtJroA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A channel link does not play in every browser. After you set the link, open /live and make sure that the stream plays. If it does not, use the watch link of each stream, for example https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=video ID, and put the new link on the Church before each service.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iOtjX2fXUR", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd12Members-only Pages", "col": 12}}, {"id": "cPHk9xRA5w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A members-only page is a page of the website that only your church's members can read. Use it for news and papers for the church family, not for the public: the agenda of a members' meeting, the annual report or budget, church policies, a newsletter, or how to get into the building.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XYTYkfPoyr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The member portal is different: each of its pages shows a person their own records. A members-only page shows the same text to every member, and you write it like any other Web Page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ywosPTEclB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "To make one, open the Web Page, tick Members Only and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "AJvVX4h-uN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Members who are signed in see the page in the menu and can open it. Only active members count.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZbfQ_2Y1Xr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Visitors who are not signed in do not see the link. If they open the address, they go to the login page and come back to the page after they sign in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "H1vKWlde1L", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- People who are signed in but are not members, for example a visitor with a portal login, do not see the link. If they open the address, they see a Not Permitted message.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "E6Fl89piuv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Staff who can edit web pages can always open it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "a9DPmqNwuF", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "People who cannot open the page never see its title in the menu, the footer, the member portal, the site map or the website search. To show a members-only page in the member portal too, add a row with its route to the Menu table in Portal Settings. In a menu, type the route exactly as the Web Page form shows it, so that the link stays hidden from visitors.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "c5A5rmKYof", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: The church secretary makes a Web Page called Annual Budget 2027 and ticks Members Only and Published. Members see Annual Budget 2027 in the menu and on the This week page of the member portal. A visitor who gets the link from a member is asked to sign in.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tkPD1LEmpv", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udd0cTurn a Website Page Off", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ph-uDekVLa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Open Church Features and open the Website Pages section. Each page that Churchit puts on the website has a row. Clear Enabled on a row and save to take that page off the website. Visitors then get \"Page not found\", its form takes no new entries, and its links go from the menu, the footer, the member portal and the site map. Nothing is deleted. Tick Enabled again to bring the page back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZFKpJSU6SN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- When you turn off a module in Church Features, its website pages go too. For example, with Study off, the sermon pages, the podcast, the Bible and Bible Memory are off.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "tVy9OkRuh8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- The Web Site module switch is different: it hides only the desk tools, and the public website stays on.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Db0N9vFm-a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Your own Web Pages are not in this list. To take one off, clear its Published box.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KybFwxpzKL", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With the Sermons, Calendar or Contact page off, the home page leaves out its links to that page. If you changed your home page yourself, check it for links to pages that are off.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "JAE5MXfaSW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "No public website", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QrBy8Dfo6b", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "If your church already has its own website, tick Turn Off the Public Website in the Website Pages section of Church Features and save. A visitor who is not signed in then sees only the login page. Members sign in and keep the member portal and the pages that are on, such as Calendar, Give and Bulletins.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "NDlT2S49kb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The pages about the church go for members too: Home, Beliefs, Sermons, Missions, Ministries, About Us, Contact Us, Locations, Watch Live, Find a Group, the Connection Card, the prayer request form for visitors, and your own Web Pages that are not Members Only.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "T9E-8rA5hS", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Visitors cannot give online or sign up for a function until they sign in. The podcast feed stays on, and the link in a ministry team request email still opens without a login. Clear the box and save to bring the website back.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "56KnUGhnDt", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: First Church already has a website made by a designer. It wants Churchit only for the member portal, online giving and the calendar. It ticks Turn Off the Public Website and puts links to /give and /calendar on its own website. Members who follow those links sign in once.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZdecGmVwdz", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udccdLocations (Multi-Church)", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ax4rjh5S1q", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When your church has more than one location, the website can show all of them. Switch on Enable Multi-Church in the Multi-Church section of Church Features (see the Foundations manual). Then open each Church and tick Publish to put it on the website. A church that you do not publish does not appear anywhere on the site.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pnTV9A7BaI", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When two or more churches are published, a Locations item appears at the end of the website menu. It lists every published church, with (selected) after the church that the page shows. All locations opens the Locations page, with a card for each church: its photo, mission statement, description and address. The photo is the Image of the Church, and visitors see it only when it is a public file (see Sermon Podcast in the Study manual for how to make an image public).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "zjCEsFKrGV", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When a visitor picks a location, the whole website switches to that church and stays there from page to page:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "iCsEmlKbK0", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- the church name in the menu, and the address and phone number in the footer,
- the home page, calendar, sermons, ministries, missions and bulletins,
- the funds offered on the Give page,
- the About Us page, which shows the About and Mission Statement of that church, or the main church's when it has none,
- anything that a visitor sends from those pages, such as a prayer request or a contact message, which goes to that church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "S6pZIRFjTD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Example: Grace Church has a main campus and a Downtown campus. Both are published. A visitor picks Downtown. The calendar shows the Downtown events, the footer shows the Downtown address, and a prayer request that the visitor sends goes to the Downtown staff.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8L-4AUmAel", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Good to know", "col": 12}}, {"id": "mGLJpJ3YVN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A record with Shared with All Churches ticked, such as a sermon, appears on the pages of every church. The Foundations manual explains sharing.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "xcjkIsx9qa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A signed-in member sees their own church first. The member portal always shows the member's own church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "p9ZC9z6l4u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A message from a branch's Contact page goes to the email of that branch. A message from the main church, or from a branch with no email, goes to Forward To Email in Contact Us Settings, or to the main church's email.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "WiX4oLOJhY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- With only one published church, or with multi-church off, there is no Locations item and no Locations page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9dxxfJu6Ke", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udcf1The App on Phones and Computers", "col": 12}}, {"id": "oZIH4zbkKM", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Members and staff can install the website as an app on a phone or a computer. The app has the name and icon of your church and opens in its own window. Under the icon, a phone shows the church name when it has 12 characters or fewer, or else the Abbreviation of the Church.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "17gz0Nou7J", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Staff open the app on the desk, and members on the member portal. Touch and hold the icon on a phone (or right-click it on a computer) to go straight to the Calendar, Prayer Request, Give or Sermons page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Vz-3vhn0oA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "After a user signs in, a card at the bottom of the page offers the app:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "qnPvuhstK_", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- On Android, and in Chrome or Edge on a computer, Install opens the install window of the browser.
- On an iPhone or iPad, the card tells the user to tap Share, then Add to Home Screen.
- Some browsers, such as Firefox on a computer, cannot install apps, so they show no card.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "PZqsV2D-7p", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Not now hides the card on that device for 30 days. A user can install the app at any time: staff click Install App in the user menu, and members click Install on the Preferences page of the member portal. To stop the card from showing by itself, clear Offer to Install the App in the App section of Church Features.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "4HlTFNdKlc", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83d\udc64Member Portal", "col": 12}}, {"id": "XrwutWucHZ", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The member portal is an app at /portal that members and staff open with their login, on a phone or a computer. It shows a person only what belongs to them or what the church shares with them. Staff who have a Person record open it from the menu at the top of the desk sidebar: choose Member Portal. Who gets a login, and how, is in the People manual.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ocEHacjftk", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A visitor who is not signed in goes to the login page. It tells them to ask the church office for a login and offers the Connection Card. Old addresses of portal pages, such as /household, open the same page in the app, so links in emails and bookmarks keep working.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "gR07Cetz7K", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The menu", "col": 12}}, {"id": "j-bYtMYa2w", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "On a computer, the menu is a column on the left. On a phone, five tabs sit at the bottom: This week, Check-in (or Sign-Ups when your church does not use self check-in), Groups, Prayer and More, which opens everything else.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "eJY2zEPl-R", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "The menu is the Menu table in Portal Settings (in the Setup folder of the Web Site sidebar). The Role on each row decides who sees it. To add, remove or rename a page in the menu, change that table. A row for a page outside the app, such as a members-only page, opens that page. A page that is turned off in Church Features leaves the menu.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "haIhJNXZHa", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "What members can do", "col": 12}}, {"id": "em44yB8CyB", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- This week: the first page. It shows what the member signed up for, when they serve and when their groups meet. When check-in is open, the first thing on the page is a button to check in. A request to serve shows the buttons Yes, I can and I can't this time. Beside the week are the bulletin's notices, the newest prayer requests with an I prayed button, the latest bulletin and the members-only pages that the member can open.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "X_b2Yl-TNu", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- My Household: the people in the household, the household photo and the address. An adult of the household can change the photo, add a child, and edit their own details and the details of their children. To add another adult or remove someone, the member asks the church office.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "b9eCs4oREY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Check-in: when your church uses self check-in, the member opens it a little before the service, chooses who is coming and taps Show our pass. Name tags print when a volunteer scans the pass at the door (see the Ministries manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "wPEA0qZ1S2", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- My Details: the member changes their name, birthday, allergies, email addresses, phone numbers and marital status, and chooses what other members see about them in the directory. The church office changes the address.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "2PmvjGYStW", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Preferences: how the member gets each kind of message, notifications on the device, the install button and light or dark mode.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "srEMSKr5BN", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Sign-Ups: Upcoming lists the member's places at functions with their status (Confirmed, Pending, Waitlisted or Cancelled). Open lists the functions that take sign-ups now. Attended is the attendance history. A function with questions or choices opens the church's sign-up page, /register. While sign-ups are open, a member can change or cancel a sign-up, and a freed place goes to the next person on the waitlist.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Lv5fWDhvcq", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Serving: where the member is asked to serve. A member can ask someone else on the team to take their place, add the dates they cannot serve, and set how often they serve (see the Ministries manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "EoDMTPuobh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Book a Room: the rooms the member asked for, and the answer to each (see the Operations manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QnQ8jcKoKA", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Groups: the member's groups, when they meet and who leads them, and the public groups of the church to join. A group's page shows who else is in it. An email or phone number shows only when that person chose to show it in the member directory. Group Files lists the files shared in the member's groups. A leader uses Groups I lead to accept people who ask to join, take attendance and message the group.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "8W0GbiLoQY", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Prayer: the member's own prayer requests and the Prayer List (see the Prayers manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "QC5rh2q9zK", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Care Requests and Benevolence Requests: ask the care team for practical or financial help, and follow the status.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "TcYiIlYebb", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Directory: the households of the church, with the details each person chose to share. Save contact adds a household to the phone.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "KyDPe6kyn1", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Bible, Bible Memory and Bulletins: read the Bible, memorize passages (see the Study manual) and read or download the bulletins.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ZDAt0HMjRP", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Pledges and Giving Statements: what the member promised to give and has given, and the yearly statements to print (see the Finances manual).", "col": 12}}, {"id": "-VF07OCapr", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "An open page updates by itself when something changes for the member, for example when a place opens on a waitlist, a child is checked in, or a leader answers a join request. The app uses the logo of the Church, and its accent color is the Primary Color of the website's Website Theme.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "sd4MXJQrE8", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\ude84Write and Translate Pages with AI", "col": 12}}, {"id": "pItGR-7Qby", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "When AI is turned on (see the Foundations manual), a saved Web Page that is published and not Members Only gets AI helpers. The AI reads only text that the public can already read. Nothing is saved until you save the page.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "1qhcBz3B1A", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Draft with AI beside Description in the Meta Tags section writes the short text that search engines show.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "CPQbYYOOzD", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Alt Text with AI in Main Section, when the Content Type is Rich Text, writes alt text for each picture that has none. Alt text is what a screen reader says for a picture. The AI cannot see the pictures: it reads the page and the file names. When they do not tell what a picture shows, it writes \"Photo from the church\". Click Use, check each text and save.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "ejrZLnPeTh", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Translate with AI makes a copy of the page in another language that is enabled on your site. Click it, choose a language and click Open Draft. A new Web Page opens, not saved and not published, with the language in brackets after its title and the language code after its address, such as about-es. Copy any JavaScript of the page yourself.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "nXwARThJ0u", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A page longer than 12000 characters cannot be translated: split it into two pages first. Churchit refuses a translation that changed the page's template code or added scripts or links to other sites.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Rma3hFpdps", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "A fluent person must check every translation. AI makes mistakes in every language, and more in a rare one. It can change the meaning of a belief or a name. Before you publish the draft, ask a person who speaks the language well, and who knows what your church believes, to read it.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "9xbNnb8wGx", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "\ud83e\uddf1Pages made with Frappe Builder", "col": 12}}, {"id": "Li4IhmZsPy", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "Frappe Builder is a separate app for designing web pages by drag and drop. A System Manager can install it next to Churchit. Before you use it, note:", "col": 12}}, {"id": "hMJhqC_P-a", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Use a Builder page only for pages that show no church records, such as a landing page. A Builder page cannot keep the records of one church apart from another. Show events, sermons or people on Churchit's pages, and link to them.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "D8-3M5xYN4", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- A Builder page takes its address before Churchit's own pages. Before you choose an address, open it in a private window, and use it only when it shows \"Page not found\". Do not use an address listed under Website Pages in Church Features, also when that page is off.", "col": 12}}, {"id": "os1q0FsQ-A", "type": "paragraph", "data": {"text": "- Churchit's shipped pages (Home, Beliefs, Missions, Ministries and Sermons) stay Web Pages.", "col": 12}}]
